_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from Kopia's documentation; no upstream egg.
name: Kopia
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Kopia is fast, encrypted, deduplicated backup. The egg runs a Kopia repository server that keeps your computers' backups in the server's folder, with its web interface behind a login.
startup: export KOPIA_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES=false KOPIA_CONFIG_PATH=/home/container/config/repository.config KOPIA_CACHE_DIRECTORY=/home/container/cache KOPIA_LOG_DIR=/home/container/logs; [ -n "{{KOPIA_PASSWORD}}" ] && [ -n "{{UI_PASSWORD}}" ] || { echo "Set Repository password and Web password first."; exit 1; }; if ! ./kopia repository status >/dev/null 2>&1; then if [ -f repository/kopia.repository.f ]; then ./kopia repository connect filesystem --path /home/container/repository || exit 1; else ./kopia repository create filesystem --path /home/container/repository || exit 1; fi; fi; if [ -n "{{CLIENT_USER}}" ] && [ -n "{{CLIENT_PASSWORD}}" ]; then ./kopia server user set "{{CLIENT_USER}}" --user-password "{{CLIENT_PASSWORD}}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ./kopia server user add "{{CLIENT_USER}}" --user-password "{{CLIENT_PASSWORD}}" || exit 1; fi; echo "Certificate fingerprint (for --server-cert-fingerprint): $(openssl x509 -in tls/server.crt -outform DER | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)"; exec ./kopia server start --address 0.0.0.0:{{SERVER_PORT}} --tls-cert-file tls/server.crt --tls-key-file tls/server.key --server-username "{{UI_USERNAME}}" --server-password "{{UI_PASSWORD}}" --disable-file-logging

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Kopia: downloads Kopia from its GitHub releases, checked against GitHub's
# SHA-256. The repository (your backups), its settings and the server's
# certificate are never touched, and the binary is only replaced once the
# new one is complete.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=x64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Kopia has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag kopia/kopia "$version") || exit 1

if [ -x kopia ] && [ "$(cat .kopia-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Kopia $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Kopia $tag"
    gh-release download kopia/kopia "$tag" "kopia-${tag#v}-linux-$arch.tar.gz" "$work/kopia.tar.gz"
    tar -xzf "$work/kopia.tar.gz" -C "$work"
    bin=$(find "$work" -type f -name kopia | head -n 1)
    [ -n "$bin" ] || fail "Kopia's download didn't have the kopia program. Reinstall to try again."
    install -m 0755 "$bin" kopia.new
    mv -f kopia.new kopia
    echo "$tag" > .kopia-version
fi
mkdir -p repository config tls
# The server's TLS certificate, made once and kept: clients trust it by its
# fingerprint, which the server prints at every start.
if [ ! -f tls/server.key ] || [ ! -f tls/server.crt ]; then
    openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:prime256v1 -nodes -days 3650 \
        -subj "/CN=kopia" -keyout tls/server.key -out tls/server.crt 2>/dev/null
    chmod 600 tls/server.key
    echo "Made the server's TLS certificate."
fi
echo "Installed Kopia $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Kopia version to install, such as 0.23.1, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Repository password
variables.description: The password that encrypts the repository, set on the first start. Keep it safe: without it the backups can't be read, and it can't be changed here later.

variables.name: Web username
variables.description: The username for the server's web interface.

variables.name: Web password
variables.description: The password for the server's web interface.

variables.name: Client user
variables.description: A computer that may back up here, as user@host (such as alex@laptop). Add more with kopia server user add.

variables.name: Client password
variables.description: The client user's password, used with kopia repository connect server.
